nodes.label: FLEX — Flame Extinguishment Experiment
nodes.description: Flammability limits of liquid fuels in microgravity and effectiveness of gaseous suppressants (CO2, He) — 274 droplet tests with measured burning rate, extinction diameter and end state.

props.hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)-Fluids and Combustion Facility (FCF), Multi-user Droplet Combustion Appartatus (MDCA)

nodes.label: BASS-II — Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
nodes.description: Ignition, flame growth, spread and extinction limits of solid fuels in low-velocity forced flow, including reduced-oxygen runs (initial O2 13.6–22.2 % vol). Data feed the combustion models used to design detection and suppression systems.

nodes.label: SAFFIRE-I — Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment-I
nodes.description: First large-scale spacecraft fire experiment, run in a Cygnus cargo vehicle after it left the ISS: how fast a large fire grows in low gravity, and how low-g flammability compares with NASA's 1-g screening test.

nodes.label: ACME BRE — Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Burning Rate Emulator
nodes.description: Burning Rate Emulator: burning of condensed-fuel surrogates in still air as a function of material properties, explicitly in NASA-considered crew atmospheres (14.7 psia/21 %, 10.2 psia/26.5 %, 8.2 psia/34 % O2).

nodes.label: BASS — Burning and Suppression of Solids
nodes.description: Flame spread and extinction over realistic solid fuels (cotton-fiberglass fabric, PMMA in several geometries, Nomex) in low-speed forced flow aboard the ISS. Built to bridge the gap between the 1-g NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 screening method and real microgravity flammability, and to test an inert gaseous extinguishing agent.

nodes.label: SAFFIRE-II — Spacecraft Fire Experiment-II
nodes.description: Flammability of several spacecraft materials in microgravity compared side-by-side with 1-g reference burns of the same samples.

nodes.label: SAME — Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment
nodes.description: Quantified the size of smoke particulate produced in low gravity and how it relates to generation and transport conditions — baseline data for spacecraft smoke-detector sensitivity.

nodes.label: FLEX-2 — Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2
nodes.description: Extends FLEX to practical and bi-component fuels over 0.5–3 atm and 17–30 % O2, including extinction mechanisms; the PSI table is a test matrix rather than a run list.

props.hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), Multi-user Droplet Combustion Appartatus (MDCA)

nodes.label: CFI — Cool Flames Investigation

props.hardware: Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA), Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)

nodes.label: ACME s-Flame — Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments-Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames

nodes.label: ACME E-FIELD Flames — Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames
nodes.description: Electric-field effects on laminar flames. Noted by the challenge as a way to mimic partial gravity through ion-driven forces — the only partial-gravity proxy in PSI.

nodes.label: SAFFIRE-III — Spacecraft Fire Experiment-III
nodes.description: Repeat of the large-scale fabric fire in a Cygnus vehicle at 30 cm/s, in concurrent and opposed flow.

nodes.label: ACME/Flame Design — Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Flame Design

nodes.label: 1-g material screening is not automatically conservative
nodes.description: Spacecraft material selection relies on NASA-STD-6001 Test 1, which ranks materials by 1-g behaviour. BASS and BASS-II were built on the hypothesis that, with adequate ventilation, materials burn as well if not better in microgravity than in normal gravity.

props.conditions: BASS / BASS-II (PSI-26, PSI-25): cm-scale fabric and PMMA samples, low-speed forced flow in the MSG.
props.limitation: Specific materials and geometries; flow and O2 per test partly only in raw files for BASS.
props.design_question: Which flow speeds and flow directions must a microgravity-relevant material test include?
props.next_validation: Extend to the materials and thicknesses of the target vehicle (SoFIE on ISS).

nodes.label: Scale matters: only SAFFIRE burned spacecraft-size samples
nodes.description: SAFFIRE-I and -III burned ~0.4 m × 0.94 m fabric samples in uncrewed Cygnus vehicles, with O2/CO2, pressure, temperature and flame-growth measurements — the only realistic-scale fire data in PSI.

props.conditions: SAFFIRE-I (PSI-98) at 20 cm/s; SAFFIRE-III (PSI-100) at 30 cm/s; concurrent and opposed flow.
props.limitation: Two samples per mission, one material (SIBAL).
props.design_question: How do fire growth and gas-concentration changes in a sealed vehicle inform detection and response time?
props.next_validation: Additional materials at exploration atmospheres (later SAFFIRE flights).

nodes.label: Stopping ventilation may not be enough in oxygen-enriched cabins
nodes.description: In quiescent microgravity, BRE flames emulating condensed materials (e.g. PMMA, nylon) kept burning quasi-steadily in the elevated-oxygen atmospheres considered for future spacecraft, whereas comparable flames at 21 % O2 self-extinguished in a short time. PSI describes these results as preliminary.

props.conditions: ACME BRE (PSI-20): porous burners 25/50 mm, CH4 or C2H4, no forced flow, O2 21–40 % in the session table.
props.limitation: Gaseous emulation of solids; per-test pressure not in the summary table; results flagged preliminary.
props.design_question: Is ventilation shutdown — an established step in fighting spacecraft fires — still a sufficient first response at 26.5–34 % O2, or must agent discharge come sooner?
props.next_validation: Burn real cabin materials at exploration atmospheres in microgravity and partial gravity (e.g. FM2).

nodes.label: Dust can look like smoke to a particle counter
nodes.description: DAFT showed that a modified commercial particle counter could be used in microgravity, measuring a test dust aerosol released on the ISS.

props.conditions: DAFT / DAFT-2 (PSI-47): 2 sessions, Arizona Road Dust in ISS nitrogen, P-Trak vs DustTrak.
props.limitation: Terrestrial test dust, not lunar regolith; feasibility test only.
props.design_question: On the Moon, regolith dust will enter habitats: how will detectors discriminate dust from smoke to avoid nuisance alarms?
props.next_validation: Characterise detector response to lunar-simulant dust versus SAME-type smoke.

nodes.label: No partial-gravity combustion data yet
nodes.description: PSI currently holds no combustion data at lunar or martian gravity. The challenge notes that microgravity and normal-gravity results can bound intermediate gravity levels, and that E-FIELD (PSI-22) mimicked partial gravity with ion-driven forces.

props.conditions: All PSI combustion investigations: microgravity (ISS, Cygnus) or ground.
props.limitation: Bounding is not interpolation: behaviour at 1/6 g may not lie between the two cases for every metric.
props.design_question: For a Moon base, which results are bounding cases and which cannot be transferred at all?

nodes.label: More oxygen: droplet flames more often survive to burnout
nodes.description: FLEX droplet tests in N2-only atmospheres that ended in flame extinction before burnout — Heptane: 5/17 at 21 % O2 vs 0/11 at 30–34 % O2; Methanol: 9/12 at 21 % O2 vs 2/13 at 30–34 % O2. Remaining tests ended in burnout ('completion') or droplet disruption.

props.conditions: FLEX (PSI-69), 274 tests, methanol and heptane droplets, O2 0.12–0.34; 103 tests near 0.7 atm (≈10.2 psia).
props.limitation: Isolated droplets, two fuels; 'extinction' here means the flame went out before the droplet was consumed (often radiative), not the action of an extinguisher. Counts, not a model.
props.design_question: How much more agent (CO2, He) or O2 depletion is needed to suppress a fire at exploration-atmosphere oxygen levels than at 21 % O2?
props.next_validation: Repeat at fixed droplet size and pressure; extend to solid cabin materials (BASS/SoFIE).

nodes.label: FLEX compares CO2 and helium as gaseous suppressants
nodes.description: At 21 % O2, share of FLEX tests ending in flame extinction before burnout by atmosphere — N2 only: 14/29; CO2: 13/18; He: 7/7. FLEX varied CO2 up to 0.7 and He up to 0.45 mole fraction.

props.conditions: FLEX (PSI-69), methanol and heptane droplets, mostly 1 atm and 0.7 atm.
props.limitation: Small samples per cell; droplet size and pressure also vary — use the Extract module to control for them.
props.design_question: Which inert agent and which concentration should a portable or fixed extinguisher deliver in a small cabin?
props.next_validation: Fit extinction diameter vs agent concentration at fixed pressure; compare with FLEX-2 and models (PSI-142).

nodes.label: Microgravity and 1-g rankings of materials can disagree
nodes.description: In SAFFIRE-II, 4 of 4 silicone samples (0.27–1.03 mm) had a burn length of about 0 in microgravity at 20 cm/s, while 2 of the 4 matching 1-g reference burns were complete. Flames did spread in microgravity over: PMMA, SIBAL (cotton-fiberglass fabric).

props.conditions: SAFFIRE-II (PSI-99): 5 cm-wide samples, 20 cm/s, ~21.5–22.1 % O2, Cygnus vehicle.
props.limitation: One test per configuration; single flow speed and near-normal O2.
props.design_question: A 1-g screening result can be optimistic for some materials (BASS hypothesis) and pessimistic for others — which materials of a given vehicle need microgravity testing?
props.next_validation: Repeat silicone at exploration-atmosphere O2 and lower flow speeds.

nodes.label: BASS-II maps solid-fuel burning down to 13.6 % O2
nodes.description: BASS-II ran 129 tests with initial O2 between 13.6 and 22.2 % vol, mostly on PMMA, SIBAL (cotton-fiberglass fabric), Nomex. Flow annotations record extinction in 15 tests, blow-off in 3 and no ignition in 1.

props.conditions: BASS-II (PSI-25), MSG flow duct, flow settings up to ~49 (display units, assumed cm/s).
props.limitation: Outcome annotations are free text; flow units to be confirmed in the BASS-II documentation; flame-spread rates are in the raw video data.
props.design_question: What O2 and flow combinations define the flammability boundary of common cabin plastics in microgravity?
props.next_validation: Extract spread rates from the raw videos for a subset (e.g. 2 cm PMMA films).
